name: GCC
summary: A multi-language compiler architecture with language front ends, shared GENERIC/GIMPLE and RTL representations, optimization passes, and target-specific back ends.

features.name: Language front-end boundary
features.description: GCC accommodates language front ends as separately organized components with language-specific source, configuration, driver integration, documentation, and preferably testsuites, which feed the common compiler infrastructure.
benefits: Allows multiple source languages to share compiler infrastructure
Keeps language-specific parsing and lowering concerns localized
costs: Each front end must coordinate build, driver, documentation, runtime, and test integration
The shared boundary must preserve language-specific semantics

features.name: Multi-stage tree and RTL representations
features.description: The GCC internals documentation describes GENERIC and GIMPLE tree representations for language-independent and SSA-oriented processing, followed by RTL for lower-level instruction-oriented work.
benefits: Gives analyses and transformations representations at different abstraction levels
Separates language-independent optimization from target-specific instruction work
costs: Lowering between representations increases compiler complexity
Information and invariants must be maintained across representation boundaries

features.name: Pass-managed optimization and target lowering
features.description: GCC documents parsing, gimplification, inter-procedural, Tree SSA, and RTL passes, while target back ends use machine descriptions and target-specific configuration to describe instruction selection and output.
benefits: Allows target-specific code generation behind a common pass pipeline
costs: Pass ordering and invalidation affect optimization outcomes
Target descriptions add portability and maintenance obligations

mathematical_views.question: How can source-language constructs be progressively lowered into forms suitable for shared optimization and target code generation?
assumptions: Each representation is modeled as a typed relation to the preceding representation
Lowering preserves the relevant semantics for the selected language and target
The view abstracts diagnostics, ABI details, and implementation-specific pass conditions

mathematical_views.question: Which analyses and transformations can be composed before target-specific lowering, and which conditions constrain their ordering?
assumptions: Passes are vertices and required ordering or data dependencies are directed edges
A pass may invalidate information computed by an earlier pass
The graph is a candidate explanatory model and does not prove equivalence of arbitrary pass sequences

benefits: Reuse of common middle-end and back-end infrastructure
costs: Front-end integration requires several coordinated repository interfaces

benefits: Specialized analyses over representations with appropriate abstraction
costs: Multiple lowering boundaries increase maintenance and source-mapping cost
Pass invalidation, ordering, and target variation complicate global reasoning
